topic: Why we see one side of the Moon
script: We always see the same side of the Moon. That is because the Moon spins exactly once for every trip around Earth. Scientists call this tidal locking. The far side is not dark; it gets just as much sunlight as the near side. No human saw it directly until the Apollo 8 crew orbited the Moon in 1968. title: Why We Only See One Side of the Moon #Moon #SpaceFacts #Shorts
description:
The Moon is tidally locked, spinning once per orbit, so one side always faces us. The far side gets just as much sunlight; Apollo 8's crew were the first people to see it.
